manifesto.title: What if the web were [[better]]?
paragraphs: Not just faster. Not just shinier. Actually [[better]] for the people using it.

Most websites look pretty and convert terribly. Agencies ship moodboards. We ship experiments. We treat your digital product like a laboratory. [[Data over opinion.]] Statistically significant growth over artistic preferences.

We refuse the hacks and deceptive design game. We reject artificial scarcity. We disavow fake urgency. Exploiting cognitive biases to trick people into decisions they will regret is a race to the bottom — and a lousy way to grow a business that wants customers to come back.

You don't need the big CRO agency. You need the [[right]] one. Research, design, build and analysis run directly — without the account-manager tax, the beer taps, or the retainer that only ever climbs.
manifesto.closer: Kill the hypothesis. Keep the revenue. Power to the users.

method.title: You don't need the big CRO agency. You need [[the lab]].
method.lead: Research, design, build and analysis — four stark steps, no proprietary fog. We explain what we're doing and why.

steps.title: DIAGNOSTIC
steps.blurb: Find what's actually broken before guessing at fixes.
steps.body: Heatmaps, user session recording analysis, analytics audit. Heuristic review. Deceptive-pattern scan. We pull the site apart and rank the leaks.

steps.title: HYPOTHESIS
steps.body: Research and evidenced hypothesis generation before a single test gets built. If it cannot be falsified, it does not ship.

steps.title: EXPERIMENTATION
steps.blurb: A/B and multivariate testing. Custom code variants.
steps.body: Variant design, copy, build, and QA. Everything required to run an experiment worth running — not a paint job with a tracking pixel.

steps.title: ITERATION
steps.body: Statistical analysis, structured learning capture, and feeding insight back into the next cycle. Winners ship. Losers die in public.

calculator.title: Run the numbers before you run the test.
calculator.lead: Drag the sliders. A 15–30% conversion lift is the band we routinely hunt. No email gate. No theatre. Just the maths.

straightTalk.title: Ethics [[first]] for results that [[last]].
straightTalk.lead: If 'growth with integrity' sounds like marketing BS to you... good. Here is what we mean.

faqs.q: What does ethical optimisation mean here?
faqs.a: Boosting conversions by removing pain and clarifying decisions — not by manipulating people. We will not ask you to ship anything you could not defend to a customer's face.

faqs.q: Won't this leave money on the table?
faqs.a: In the shortest term you could squeeze a few extra sales by confusing people. Then you lose the ones who work out they have been had. The ethics-versus-results trade-off is a fiction sold by people whose model depends on hacks.

faqs.q: What if we ask for something you won't do?
faqs.a: We will say why, then offer an alternative aimed at the same business goal. Fake countdown timers and hidden opt-outs are not a strategy. They are a confession.

Businesses that care whether customers come back. If you sell something useful and would rather grow through respect than through tricks, we will get on. If your model depends on misleading people, we are not the lab.

items.title: Out of Step
items.body: Your funnel has problems (maybe). Some are fixable in a day. Some go deeper. We find them, rank them, test them, and kill the ones that fail.

items.title: No More Heroes
items.body: The industry runs on mystification — frameworks dressing up the same practice as proprietary method. We explain what we're doing and why.

items.title: Ever been cheated?
items.body: Fake urgency. Hidden opt-outs. Consent theatre. We identify every manipulative pattern, explain the cost, and propose replacements that still convert.

caseStudies.title: Before. After. [[Evidence.]]
caseStudies.lead: Interactive toggles. Real conversion experiments. No vanity screenshots, no "we increased engagement" fog.

studies.note: Redesigned checkout flow. Hypothesis: reduce steps and expose guest checkout. Result: +42% lift in paid conversion. Fake urgency was not part of the variant.
High-intent landing page overhaul. Hypothesis: match message to keyword and kill the carousel. Result: −30% CAC. Same media spend. Better users, not cheaper tricks.
